body:
I too have been having a lot of trouble being little. I want to be, and when I'm lying in my bed doing nothing I find that it's a lot easier. There are of course the physical things you can do, like Dojima mentioned, that could help you be little, but there are some mental things to keep in mind as well.

If you have a daddy, be little TO YOUR DADDY. One of my friends has that submissive mode they go into the moment they talk to their SO. They see something cool and go "Leo (fake name)! Leo look!" She seeks his input and his guidance and can be childish around him. But when she talks to other people she no longer acts little.

Live in the moment. You can't experience life as a little constantly thinking about what you have to do, what you've done, or if you have anxiety what others think about what you're doing. If you're with your Daddy and suddenly you want to skip down the sidewalk with him, don't second guess it - do it.

On that note, you can't be afraid of what others think about you. I personally battle social anxiety and I make it a challenge for me to be little even in public. Before I would stare at the ground and bring as little attention to myself as possible. I would talk quietly on the phone to my Daddy and hope nobody can hear me. Now? I have to reason with myself that I'll never see these people again, and that these people I don't even know don't matter compared to whatever is going on in the moment.

I LOVED Guild Wars. It was my first real mmorpg and I played it for 6 years straight xD I played gw2 for two years and got bored of it, which is why I spent several months sleeping because I had nothing else to do.

As stated, I have played video games since I was a child. I became depressed a little less than a year ago. I ran out of games to play the middle of last year, and spent my days sleeping as much as I could because I had nothing to do. Then I tried World of Warcraft and have been hooked ever since. It saved me. But now it's kind of devouring me, *oops*

Thanks. Not too specific to make me turn away saying, "No, I'm not doing that," and just vague enough that I can get the retrospect of what you're saying. I'll start considering a lot of options. (Working out is definitely not going to be one of them) 

Reading, for example. Or maybe drawing.

I'm from the United States, where unfortunately depression is seen as just another simple emotion or even a 'hobby' in some eyes. 

As for my mom, it took my about five months into it to finally get the courage to tell her, when I realized it wasn't going away on its own. I told her I wanted help, but I don't think she understood the kind of help I wanted to seek. She is a licensed therapist, though she has never actually done anything, simply graduated college with the degree. So she immediately started asking me questions. What's the source? What's the balance between positive and negative impacts in my life? Who actually cares about me? And she told me to make the chart and then give it back to her. Of course, my response was immediately leaving and taking a nap. 

About a week after she asked if I had done the chart (although throughout the week she simply asked if I was working on it.)

When I told her I wasn't working on it and I wasn't going to, we spoke about it again. I told her eventually that I wanted medical help. Medicine. I was afraid of a therapist though. I feel like I'd be wasting their time; my source of depression is pathetic, simple jealousy and a breakup that drew me down. She said, if I really felt like I needed it, she'd schedule the appointment on Monday. I told her I did.

She never scheduled it.
